raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

The example Helm chart probed `/health`, which only reports whether the engine process is alive. It does not generate text, so a hung but alive engine still looked healthy. This PR makes the chart's startup, readiness and liveness probes check that the model actually returns text. It makes no change to vLLM code.

## Claims

- The default startup, readiness and liveness probes send a one-token completion (`/v1/completions`, `max_tokens: 1`, `temperature: 0`) and succeed only if the response contains non-empty text.
- A new `probeRequest` value defines the request once for all three probes.
- Users can override any probe with their own handler, for example `httpGet /health`. The chart keeps it as is.
- Nothing under `vllm/` is modified.

## Validation

- `helm lint .` passes.
- `helm unittest .` passes (13 tests, 3 new).

## Details

- Each probe uses GPU time and competes with user traffic. The liveness defaults are therefore tolerant (period 30s, timeout 30s, failure threshold 6), and the startup probe allows 120 attempts every 10s. The docs describe the `/health` fallback.
- The probes send no credentials, so they do not work when the server runs with `--api-key`. This is documented.
- `probeRequest.model` must match `--served-model-name`.

+## Probes
+
+By default, the chart checks that the model actually answers text, not only that the engine process is alive. The startup, readiness and liveness probes run an `exec` command inside the container that sends the `probeRequest` (a one-token completion with `temperature: 0`) to the local server with `curl`. The probe succeeds only if the response contains a non-empty `text`.
+
+```yaml
+probeRequest:
+  endpoint: /v1/completions
+  model: opt-125m # must match --served-model-name
+  prompt: "Hello"
+  maxTokens: 1
+```
+
+Things to be aware of:
+
+- Each probe generates tokens, so it uses GPU time and competes with user traffic. The defaults are tolerant (long liveness period and timeout, `failureThreshold: 6`) so that a busy pod is not restarted prematurely. Tune them to your workload.
+- The probes send no credentials. They do not work when the server runs with `--api-key`, because `/v1/*` is protected. Override the probes with `httpGet` on `/health` in that case.
+- The image must provide `curl` and `grep`. The official `vllm/vllm-openai` image does.
+- `probeRequest.model` must match the name served by the container (`--served-model-name`).
+
+To use a different check for a probe, set your own handler. The chart then keeps it as is instead of generating the `exec` probe. For example, to fall back to the lightweight engine health check for liveness:
+
+```yaml
+livenessProbe:
+  httpGet:
+    path: /health
+    port: 8000
+  initialDelaySeconds: 15
+  periodSeconds: 10
+  timeoutSeconds: 5
+  failureThreshold: 3
+```
+

+## Probes that check the model answers
+
+The `/health` endpoint only reports whether the engine process is alive. It does not generate any token, so a hung but alive engine still reports healthy. To make Kubernetes check that the model answers text, use an `exec` probe that sends a one-token completion with `curl` and succeeds only if the generated text is not empty:
+
+```yaml
+readinessProbe:
+  exec:
+    command:
+    - /bin/sh
+    - -c
+    - >-
+      curl -s --max-time 9 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$1"
+      http://localhost:8000/v1/completions
+      | grep -Eq '"text": *"[^"]'
+    - model-probe
+    - '{"model":"mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3","prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":1,"temperature":0}'
+  periodSeconds: 10
+  timeoutSeconds: 10
+  failureThreshold: 3
+```
+
+!!! note
+    - Each probe consumes GPU time and competes with user traffic. For liveness, use a long `periodSeconds`, `timeoutSeconds` and `failureThreshold`, or keep `httpGet` on `/health`, so a busy pod is not restarted.
+    - `/v1/*` endpoints are protected by `--api-key`, so this probe does not work with an API key unless you add the `Authorization` header.
+    - The `model` field must match the model name or `--served-model-name`.
+    - The image must provide `curl` and `grep`.
+
+The [Helm chart](frameworks/helm.md#probes) uses this approach by default.
+
